Roofing in Mesquite, Texas

Much of Mesquite was built in a hurry between 1950 and 1970, and the city has its own licensing step before a roofer can get a permit. Call one free number to reach an independent roofing company that serves Mesquite.

Call (469) 649-7066 Mesquite license and permit steps
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Mesquite

Twenty years that built most of Mesquite

To understand roofing in Mesquite, TX, start with a census table. The town counted 1,696 people in 1950. By 1960 it had 27,526, and by 1970 it had 55,131.

That growth came from returning veterans and a housing shortage in Dallas, and it was met with block after block of new single-story homes. The roads and water lines had to catch up, and so did everything else. By about 1970 the LBJ Freeway, I-635, linked Mesquite with Garland and Balch Springs, and Town East Mall opened in 1971. The Mesquite Championship Rodeo, which began as a professional rodeo in 1958, gave the town its nickname as the Rodeo Capital of Texas.

A house framed in 1958 has lived through more than sixty North Texas summers. Its original roof is long gone, and it has almost certainly been re-roofed more than once. The questions a homeowner should ask on a roof that old are different from the questions on a 2010 build, and they start under the shingles: the condition of the decking, whether old layers were ever removed, and how the attic breathes.

Most of the city sits in Dallas County, with a small part reaching into Kaufman County. Both sides fall under the same City of Mesquite building rules.

Mesquite's license step comes before the permit

Mesquite handles contractors a little differently from many neighbors. The city's building FAQ puts it plainly: a professional license is required before a building permit can be issued.

The professional license

Contractors get it through the city's online Citizen Self Service portal. It is a city license, not a state one; Texas itself does not license roofers. Ask any company you are considering whether its Mesquite license is active.

Who can apply for permits

The portal accepts permit applications from licensed contractors, and from homeowners who own the house, live in it and carry a homestead exemption with the Dallas Central Appraisal District. For roof work, let the roofer apply.

What needs a permit

The city lists new construction, repairs, remodels, windows and exterior doors among permitted work and exempts cosmetic jobs like paint and carpet. Its rental inspection checklist names roofs, with inspections booked through the portal.

Who to ask

Mesquite Building Inspection answers at 972-216-6212, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Rules and fees change, so ask about your exact job before work begins.

The Saturday morning tornado of March 2019

At about 7:35 a.m. on Saturday, March 9, 2019, residents near Allen Drive heard rain, then hail, then a roar. The National Weather Service surveyed the damage and confirmed an EF-0 tornado, the weakest rating, with winds estimated at 75 to 85 mph. It tracked from the Allen Drive and Cedar Crest area east across I-635 and south Belt Line Road before lifting near Wilkinson and Paza.

Weak as it was, it took roofs. Homes on Allen Drive lost shingles and fences, one family's house was made unlivable, and part of the roof of a church blew off, with metal landing on the freeway. Police reported no injuries.

Most Mesquite roof damage comes from storms less dramatic than that one: spring wind, hail and long rain. The pattern after any of them is the same. Look from the yard, photograph what you see, call your insurer, then get a roofer to look up close.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Before you sign with a Mesquite roofer

  • Ask whether the company's City of Mesquite professional license is current, and whose name will be on the permit.
  • On a house from the 1950s or 1960s, ask how many old layers are up there and whether the price strips every one to bare wood.
  • Have the roofer explain how air enters and leaves the attic now, and what the new roof will change about it.
  • Ask what replacing a damaged sheet of decking will add to the bill, and ask to see photos of any sheet before it is swapped.
  • Request a certificate of liability insurance mailed or emailed to you by the insurer, not a photocopy.
  • Get the workmanship warranty and the shingle maker's warranty registration in writing.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

Mesquite roofing questions

How do I find roofers in Mesquite TX who can pull a permit?

Ask each company whether it holds a City of Mesquite professional license. The city says that license must be in place before anyone can get a building permit, and contractors apply for it through Mesquite's Citizen Self Service portal. A company without one cannot permit your job. Callers to the free line reach an independent local roofer; put that question to it too before you sign anything. More checks are in the roofer checking guide.

Does Mesquite require a permit for roof work?

Mesquite's building FAQ says permits are required for new construction, repairs, remodels, windows, exterior doors and similar work, and that purely cosmetic jobs such as paint, carpet or cabinets are exempt. A roof is not cosmetic. The city's own rental inspection checklist lists roofs as permitted work, with inspections scheduled in its online portal. Confirm the details for your job with Building Inspection at 972-216-6212.

Can a Mesquite homeowner pull the roofing permit instead of the roofer?

Mesquite allows a homeowner who occupies the house and holds a homestead exemption with the Dallas Central Appraisal District apply for permits. That rule is for paperwork, not a reason to do roof work yourself. Roofs are dangerous, and the company doing the job should hold the Mesquite license and pull the permit in its own name, so the inspection and the responsibility sit with the people on the roof.

Has a tornado hit Mesquite?

Yes. On the morning of March 9, 2019, the National Weather Service confirmed an EF-0 tornado with winds of 75 to 85 mph in Mesquite. It began near Allen Drive and Cedar Crest, crossed I-635 and Belt Line Road, and lifted near Wilkinson and Paza. Roofs and fences on Allen Drive were damaged, one home was left unlivable, and a church lost part of its roof. No injuries were reported.

Is DFW Expert Roofers a roofing company in Mesquite?

It is not a roofing company anywhere. It is a free number. Its automated assistant answers around the clock, hears the trouble with your roof and your Mesquite address, and transfers you to an independent, locally owned roofer serving the area. The roofer does the inspecting, pricing and work, and bills you itself. The roofer you reach can pay the line a fee for sending you. Read how calls are handled.

Talk to a roofer who works in Mesquite

Say what the roof is doing and which town you are in. The automated assistant passes you to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in DFW. That company comes out, looks at the roof and prices the job itself.
